summary:
NISAR ChangeLens is an interactive web-based tool that helps users explore and interpret changes in Earth's surface using NASA-ISRO NISAR radar data. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Dancing with the SARs,” the project focuses on a pilot area in Vietnam's Mekong Delta.

Users can explore satellite data coverage, select areas of interest, compare two NISAR Global Coherence and Backscatter (GCOV) observations, and visualize changes in radar backscatter through an interactive map and Before/After comparison. A scientific evidence system checks data compatibility and coverage before allowing comparisons.

By making complex SAR observations easier to explore, NISAR ChangeLens aims to support more accessible Earth observation analysis and help users investigate environmental changes. It emphasizes transparent data provenance, reproducible processing, and responsible interpretation rather than treating radar backscatter changes as definitive proof of flooding or land-cover change.
details:
NISAR ChangeLens is an interactive web application developed to make NASA-ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations easier to explore and interpret.

The project focuses on the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, where changes in water distribution and surface conditions are important for understanding environmental dynamics. Users can explore a map, inspect NISAR data catalog coverage, select an area of interest, and compare two temporally separated NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) observations. The application visualizes gamma-zero backscatter in decibels and its temporal difference through map overlays and an interactive Before/After comparison.

A scientific compatibility system evaluates observation metadata, acquisition geometry, polarization, spatial alignment, valid-pixel coverage, and other requirements before enabling a comparison. The pilot analysis uses two real NISAR observations acquired on October 22 and November 3, 2026, over an approximately 120.77 km² area in An Giang, Vietnam, with 99.9065% common valid-pixel coverage.

The processing workflow uses Python and geospatial libraries to extract and process raster data, apply a mask-aware 5×5 boxcar filter to linear radar power, convert gamma-zero power to decibels, and calculate temporal differences. The web interface uses TypeScript, React, and MapLibre GL JS, with an English/Vietnamese language selector.

The project's creative contribution is its combination of an interactive map, transparent data provenance, automated scientific compatibility checks, and clear warnings about interpretation. Backscatter changes can indicate variations in surface conditions, but do not independently prove flooding or land-cover change.

NISAR ChangeLens was built with reproducibility and responsible use in mind. It provides a verified local pilot dataset so users can explore the demonstration without requiring their own NASA Earthdata credentials. The project aims to make advanced radar observations more accessible to students, researchers, and people interested in environmental monitoring.
